data.one_liner: Cross-platform on-device LLM inference for GGUF and LiteRT-LM models.
data.what_it_does: Runs GGUF (llama.cpp) and LiteRT-LM models locally across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and the web. Provides text generation, chat streaming, structured JSON output, tool calling, embeddings, and multimodal capabilities behind a unified API.
use_when: You need on-device, offline LLM inference in Dart or Flutter.
You want to run GGUF or LiteRT-LM models locally on mobile, desktop, or web.
You require advanced LLM features like tool calling, structured JSON output, or multimodal inputs.
avoid_when: Your application relies entirely on cloud-based LLM APIs and requires no local execution.
Target device resources are too limited to run local models effectively.
strengths: Cross-platform support including mobile, desktop, and web.
Supports multiple runtimes like llama.cpp and LiteRT-LM through a shared engine API.
Includes features like streaming chat, tool calling, LoRA adapters, and multimodal input.
weaknesses: Requires managing large model files on device storage.
Web support is experimental and requires specific setup.
data.setup_notes: Requires platform-specific deployment target configurations (such as iOS 16.4+ and macOS 14.0+) and adding companion packages or running build hooks/setup scripts depending on the target.

alternatives.name: firebase_ai
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose firebase_ai if you prefer using cloud-hosted Gemini models instead of running local on-device models.

alternatives.name: tflite_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose tflite_flutter if you want generic TensorFlow Lite machine learning inference rather than specialized LLM and GGUF orchestration.
